analysis:
Both supplied units are test-only code in provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/KVCacheSSD/SSDPrefixCacheTests.swift. Unit :9 is base lines 4238-4588, covering sliding-window sidecar tests. These tests check the replay bound, endurance ordering, TTL refresh, and that the plaintext header hides the absolute position through an HMAC commitment, which relates to T-041 leak #2. Unit :10 is head lines 1-609, covering fixtures and the HMAC tag, DBK3, AAD tamper, symlink and race tests. Neither unit falls in the changed range.

The complete range map shows that the only change is a head-side insertion at lines 3140-3240. That insertion adds SSDWholeRootMaintainer tests. One verifies that a header corrupted after an earlier pass loses its ownership proof even when its mtime is restored, using ctime/verdict memoization. Another verifies that a replaced lookalike is re-read on the next pass.

These additions imply that the source side, SSDWholeRootMaintainer, caches header verdicts keyed by file identity, size, mtime and ctime. That source is not in this batch.

Integration should verify the following in the maintainer source change:
- the verdict cache cannot let a file whose ownership was proven earlier keep that ownership after its contents are swapped by a same-UID operator (TB-003/T-041), since that could lead to deleting non-owned files or skipping eviction;
- inode, dev, ctime and size are all in the cache key;
- the cache is bounded in memory.

The test-only changes themselves introduce no regression and do not weaken the threat-model controls (HMAC names, AAD binding, TTL, symlink rejection).
